title: How to replace an actor in a video without reshooting
summary: Replace an actor with an authorized reference image, choose character replace vs face swap, review difficult frames, and finish audio or VFX safely.
body_markdown:
Quick Answer


## Quick answer


**To replace an actor without reshooting, upload the existing clip and an authorized reference image to Magic Hour Character Replace, generate one short representative shot, then review identity, motion, hands, occlusion and background continuity across the full clip.** Use face swap when only the face should change; use manual VFX when the shot requires frame-level control.


This workflow changes generated pixels, not contracts or permissions. Obtain rights to the source footage, performance, likeness, voice, music and final commercial use. Disclose a synthetic or materially altered person when the distribution context requires it.

## When actor replacement is a good fit


-


**Ad and campaign variants.** Keep the approved shot and test a different authorized spokesperson or character.


-


**Casting and previsualization.** Explore a look in an existing performance before committing to a shoot or VFX build.


-


**Training updates.** Replace an unavailable presenter, then separately review the script, voice and lip sync.


-


**Stylized transformations.** Turn a visible person into an authorized illustrated, animated or fictional character while retaining the source performance as the guide.


Use a manual compositing workflow when people overlap, the subject leaves frame, foreground objects cross the body, lighting changes sharply, hands interact with props, the camera cuts frequently, or every frame must satisfy a broadcast or VFX delivery standard.


## What to prepare before you start


-


**Source clip.** Begin with one continuous representative shot. Cleaner visibility, less motion blur and fewer occlusions make failures easier to diagnose.


-


**Reference image.** Use a sharp, well-lit image where the replacement character is clearly visible. Match angle, framing and lighting to the source when possible.


-


**Acceptance checklist.** Define which identity cues, wardrobe details, products, background elements, actions and timing must remain correct.


-


**Rights record.** Keep written permission for every real person's likeness and voice plus the source footage and distribution use.


-


**Fallback plan.** Decide whether a failed shot will be simplified, cut, masked or handed to a VFX artist.


## How to replace an actor step by step


### 1. Select Replace or Animate


Open[Magic Hour Character Replace](https://magichour.ai/products/character-replace) . Use Replace when an existing video supplies the performance. Animate is a different starting route and should not be treated as the same edit.


### 2. Upload the source video


Choose the shot containing the primary subject. Test the hardest representative motion early rather than processing an entire sequence before discovering that an interaction or occlusion fails.


### 3. Add the reference image


Upload the authorized person or character image that defines the new appearance. Avoid tiny, blurred, heavily filtered or obstructed references. A closer match in lighting and viewpoint gives the system a clearer constraint.


### 4. Choose Character or Scene mode


Use Character mode when the source background, timing and camera movement should remain the anchors. Scene mode regenerates the broader frame and is appropriate only when changing the whole look is intentional.


### 5. Generate one representative shot


Keep the source, reference and settings fixed for the first few attempts. The current product page says the browser tool can be tried without signup with three free generations per day; free results may include a watermark, and paid plans permit commercial use. Recheck the linked page because allowances and plan terms can change.


### 6. Review the full clip


Watch at normal speed and frame by frame around difficult moments. Check face and body identity, silhouette, hair, hands, clothing, product geometry, contact with props, shadows, reflections, camera motion, background continuity, flicker and drift.


### 7. Finish audio and compositing separately


Approve the visual replacement before changing dialogue. Use[Lip Sync](https://magichour.ai/products/lip-sync) for authorized new audio, then verify exact words, names, numbers, timing and mouth movement. For masks, edge repair or foreground occlusion, use a manual compositor such as[Adobe After Effects](https://www.adobe.com/products/aftereffects/rotoscoping.html) .


## Character replace vs face swap


Character Replace changes the primary subject's broader appearance while using the source motion and scene as anchors.[Face Swap Video](https://magichour.ai/products/face-swap/video) changes the face while retaining the original body, hair, wardrobe and performance. Choose the narrower operation whenever it satisfies the brief; it preserves more of the original shot.


## How to evaluate cost and quality


**Cost per accepted shot = all generation charges + rejected attempts + review and correction time + finishing costs, divided by approved shots.**


Retain the source, reference, settings and every output. A technically completed generation is not an accepted shot. Record why each rejection occurred so you can determine whether a better reference, simpler source, different operation or manual VFX path fixes the problem.

AI character replacement generates a new subject guided by the source clip and reference. Rotoscoping and compositing let an artist define masks, tracking, mattes, layers and corrections frame by frame. Manual work costs more time but gives precise control over difficult shots.
